note: Written from how the program actually runs. Every claim here has to match the offer lock in companies/gridschool-phase0; if the offer changes, this file changes in the same commit.

terms.title: Terms
terms.lede: Plain terms for a program run by one person. If anything here reads as a trick, tell me and I will fix the wording rather than hide behind it.

sections.heading: What you are buying
body: There are three plans. Free: your map from the free check, today's step, the check's questions, and the first two course modules (profile images, and your headline, About and top roles) with their films. GridSchool Complete: the whole course and every film, your map and the system that keeps it current, and the first week's work prepared for you (roles that fit your map, who to reach on each team, and a short note to each in your voice), plus tools that draft your resume, headshot, banner, project ideas and posts from your own answers and work. Complete runs on its own: drafts are made by software from what you tell us, and you decide what to send. The GridSchool Residency: everything in Complete, plus calls with me twice a week for the first eight weeks, building the projects that make you stand out together, then a weekly 45-minute one-to-one on your search until you sign an offer, for up to 12 months from your start.

It is coaching, a course and software. It is not a bootcamp, not a degree, not accredited, and not a recruiting or employment agency: I do not place you in a job or have access to jobs that you don't.

sections.heading: What I do not promise
body: I do not promise that a company hires you. Nobody honest can. None of these plans is a job-or-refund, an income share agreement, or a guaranteed interview, and none charges anything after you are hired. In the Residency, after week 8 I keep the weekly one-to-one, interview preparation from your own work, and help getting eyes on the evidence until you sign an offer or 12 months from your start, whichever comes first. That is a service I keep providing. It is not a promise that a company says yes.
Students who enrolled before these plans keep the agreements they signed.
I do not give legal, immigration, visa, or tax advice.

sections.heading: Who this is for
body: You must already be able to build something that runs end to end. If you cannot yet, the application will say so and turn you down, because taking your money would waste months of your life and earn a refund request.

sections.heading: Price and payment
body: Free costs nothing and asks for no card.

GridSchool Complete is $997 once, for 12 months. Or it is a monthly plan: 7 days free, then $97 a month, charged to your card on the same day each month until you cancel, and never more than 12 payments ($1,164) in all. The monthly plan's terms are shown next to its button and again at checkout before you agree. We email you 3 days before the trial ends and the first charge is made. If you cancel during the trial, you are not charged.
The GridSchool Residency is $12,000 in one payment, or 3 monthly payments of $4,000 that stop after the third. Either way it is one fixed price, with nothing hourly and nothing after you are hired.

Prices are in US dollars and include any sales tax, VAT or GST we are required to collect, so the price shown is the price you pay. If you are outside the US, checkout can show and charge the price in your own currency at the checkout partner's exchange rate; your card's own conversion then doesn't apply.
Payments are handled by the checkout partner named on the checkout page (Stripe). I never see or store your card details.

sections.heading: Cancelling and refunds
body: Complete, paid once: ask within 14 days of paying and you get a full refund, no questions asked. Reply to any email from us.

Complete, monthly: cancel any time, online, from the link in your emails (it opens the checkout partner's own billing page), or by replying to any email from us; it is done the same day. You keep your map and the course until the end of the month you paid for, then your seat pauses. Nothing is deleted, so you can restart later where you left off.
The Residency: the week 2 exit below.

sections.heading: Gifts
body: You can buy GridSchool Complete or the Residency for someone else, usually a son or daughter. A gift is paid once; nothing renews on your card. The person receiving it must be 18 or older.

Nothing is made for them until they accept it from the link in their own email. If they decline, you are refunded in full. Once they accept, the plan is theirs, under these terms, and the refund rules above apply as if they had bought it, with the refund going to your card.

When they accept, they choose whether you get a short weekly progress note: steps finished, notes and applications sent, replies, and what's next. You never see what is said on calls, their drafts, or my reviews of their work. Either of you can stop the notes from the link in any of them.

sections.heading: The week 2 exit
body: In the Residency, if either of us says this is the wrong room by the end of week 2, unused tuition comes back. No essay required. If you chose 3 payments, the later payments are cancelled.
This is the Residency's only guarantee, and it is deliberate: it covers the risk you cannot judge yet, which is whether we work well together.

sections.heading: The quota, and what happens if it stops
body: The Residency's quota is work every day, a ship URL every week, and the calls you booked. Application volume and LinkedIn posting are not requirements.

Miss three weeks of ship or three calls and your seat pauses and I call you. If we agree it is over, it ends; if not, it resumes at your pace. Eight weeks is the build phase, not a hire-by date. After week 8 the weekly one-to-one continues until you sign an offer or 12 months from your start; once you have landed a position, I stay reachable.

sections.heading: Your side of it
body: Show up to the sessions you booked. Submit real work, not work someone else wrote for you. Be honest about where a model helped you: the point is to be able to defend the code, and I cannot teach that if the trail is fake.
You are responsible for what you apply to, what you say in interviews, and what you ship.

sections.heading: Your work stays yours
body: You own the code you write and the profile you build. Contributions to the shared studio repository are made under that repository's licence.
I will not publish your work, your reviews, or your name as a case study without asking you first.

sections.heading: Materials and the room
body: Recordings, prompt packs, review documents, and the curriculum are for you, for as long as you are in the program. Do not resell them or republish them as your own.
The Discord room is for people in the program. Harassment, spam, recruiting other members into your own offer, or leaking other people's work in progress ends your access.

sections.heading: Ending it
body: You can stop at any time. In the Residency, after week 2 tuition is non-refundable because the seat is one of three and I cannot fill it mid-way; if you chose 3 payments, the remaining ones are still due.
I can end any plan with a refund of unused tuition if you break the conduct rules above, or if I cannot deliver what I sold.

sections.heading: YouTube
body: Parts of GridSchool's tools use YouTube API Services. Anyone using those tools agrees to the YouTube Terms of Service (https://www.youtube.com/t/terms) and acknowledges the Google Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy).

sections.heading: Changes
body: If these terms change, the effective date at the top changes with them and anyone currently enrolled keeps the terms they enrolled under for their cohort.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lede: A short, honest description of what is collected and who touches it. There is no data business here; the data exists so the program can run.

sections.heading: What I collect
body: From the application: your name, email, links to your work and profile, and your written answers about what you have shipped and what you think is blocking you.

If you answer an ad or message GridSchool: your name, the email and phone you give, your Instagram or Facebook account id, the messages we exchange, your answers on the ad's form, which ad you came from, and whether you booked or attended a call.

From the free check: your answers to its questions, the email you give if you ask us to send you your map, and where you came from (for example, the video). If you add your resume, its text is sent once to the AI provider that reads it (currently Anthropic or xAI, through their business APIs) and is not stored. We keep only what the read found, such as the job titles your experience supports.
From the program: your board, meaning the URLs you attach as evidence, task state, review requests and the written reviews I return, and your weekly quota numbers.
That is all. No tracking profile, no data enrichment, nothing bought from a third party.

sections.heading: Why
body: To decide whether the program fits you, to run the residency, and to know where you are so a review is useful.

Your email and phone are used to talk to you about the program you asked about: replies, follow-ups, and reminders for calls you booked. If you don't enrol, I may email you about the program a few more times; every email has a one-click unsubscribe. No newsletter, and no list sold or rented to anyone.

sections.heading: Where it lives
body: While the platform is pre-backend, your board lives in your own browser's storage and in a file I keep in the project repository when you or I export it. Nothing about your board is sent to a third-party analytics service.
Lead details and messages are kept in my own database on a private server I rent.

Services that see only what they need: Meta (ads, lead forms, Instagram and Messenger), HighLevel (the messaging service that carries texts, emails and direct messages), Calendly (bookings), Fathom (call notes), the checkout partner named on the checkout page (payments), Discord (the room), Telegram (where I'm notified about new messages), and my mail provider.

sections.heading: Messages, and the assistant that helps answer them
body: Replies to Instagram, Facebook, text and email messages are written with the help of an AI assistant I set up. It works only from facts I wrote and approved, it never claims to be a person, and if you ask whether you're talking to a bot it tells you. I read the conversations and I take every call myself.
To write a reply, the text of the conversation is sent to the AI providers that run the assistant (currently Anthropic and xAI) through their business APIs. Nothing is sent to them for advertising.

sections.heading: Text messages
body: You only get texts if you ticked the box agreeing to them. The details are on the text message terms page: what you'll get, how often, and how to stop.

Mobile numbers and text message consent are never shared with or sold to third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes. The messaging service and its carrier partners handle your number only to deliver the texts.
Reply STOP to any text and the texts end, along with the other follow-ups.

sections.heading: What I never do
body: I do not sell your data. I do not share your application or your reviews with recruiters, employers, or anyone else without you asking me to.
I do not use your private work as marketing without your written permission.

If someone gave you GridSchool as a gift, they get a weekly progress note only if you agree when you accept it, and it holds only counts and step titles (what you finished, how many notes and applications you sent, replies, what's next). You can stop it any time from the link in your welcome email.

sections.heading: How long I keep it
body: Applications I turn down are deleted within ninety days. If you enrol, your board and review history are kept while you are in the program and for a year after it ends, because a reference request later is common and the record is what makes it credible.

If you messaged me or filled in a form and didn't enrol, your messages and details are deleted within twelve months of our last contact. If you opted out, I keep only your number or email and the date, so you are never contacted again.
A free check you saved is kept with your lead details and deleted on the same schedule: within twelve months of our last contact if you don't enrol, or sooner if you ask.
Ask me to delete any of it earlier and I will, except for what I am required to keep for payment records.

sections.heading: Your say over it
body: Email me and you can have a copy of everything I hold about you, a correction, or deletion. One person reads that inbox, so you get an answer from a human rather than a ticket.

sections.heading: Cookies and measurement
body: The site sets no cookies and uses no third-party analytics. The free check counts its own steps (opened, started, finished, saved, signed in) under a random id kept in your browser, along with where you came from (for example, the video), so we can see which parts work and which don't. It keeps no IP address and nothing you type. The app uses your browser's local storage to remember which board you are on and any changes you have not exported yet. Clearing site data clears it.

When you're signed in to the app, it records how you use it, so I can see where it's confusing and fix it: which screens you open and for how long, which buttons and controls you use, the warnings and errors you run into, and when you leave. It never records what you type, only which box or button you used. This is tied to your account, kept for 180 days, and seen only by me; it isn't shared with or sent to any third party.
whenAdTracking: Advertising measurement is active: an ad platform pixel records that you visited and whether you applied, so I can tell which ads bring people who are actually a fit. It does not receive your application answers or your board.
You can block it with any tracker blocker and the site keeps working.

sections.heading: YouTube data
body: GridSchool's internal research tool uses YouTube API Services. By using it, you agree to be bound by the YouTube Terms of Service (https://www.youtube.com/t/terms), and Google's Privacy Policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy) applies to the data YouTube holds.

What it accesses: public information about public YouTube videos and channels (titles, tags, thumbnails, view, like and comment counts, subscriber counts), and, with the channel owner's sign-in, the analytics of GridSchool's own channel. It does not access any viewer's account or personal data.

How it is used: to see which topics and packaging styles perform well relative to each channel's usual videos, so GridSchool can decide what to make next. The ratios and image measurements it produces are our own calculations, not YouTube metrics. Nothing is sold or shared, and nothing is shown publicly.

Storage and deletion: titles, channel names and thumbnails are refreshed or deleted within 30 days. Statistics and our derived measurements are kept only as long as YouTube's developer policies allow (30 days, or up to 36 months where YouTube has approved that use). Data about a video that is deleted or made private is removed at the next refresh. The tool stores no cookies or other data on anyone's device.
GridSchool's own channel access can be revoked at any time at https://security.google.com/settings/security/permissions. To ask about or delete any YouTube data we hold, email support@gridschool.org.

sections.heading: Age
body: This program is for adults. Do not apply if you are under 18.

sms.title: Text messages
sms.lede: What you agreed to if you ticked the box to get texts from GridSchool, and how to stop them.

sections.heading: What you'll get
body: Texts from GridSchool (GRID SCHOOL LLC) about the program you asked about: replies to your questions, follow-ups, and reminders for calls you booked. Some are sent automatically. Nothing from anyone else.

sections.heading: How often
body: Message frequency varies: usually a few texts around a conversation or a booked call, then nothing. Message and data rates may apply.

sections.heading: Stopping, and help
body: Reply STOP to any text. You get one confirmation and no more texts, and the other follow-ups stop too.
Reply HELP, or email inquire@gridschool.org, and a person answers.

sections.heading: Not required
body: Agreeing to texts is not a condition of applying, booking a call, or enrolling.

sections.heading: Your number
body: Your number and your consent are never shared with or sold to anyone for marketing. See the privacy page for everything else.
Carriers are not liable for delayed or undelivered messages.
